From onboarding to the ledger, one connected flow

The same sequence your team already runs, with each step feeding the next so stock and accounts stay in step.

  1. Admin portal

    Step 1: Distributor onboarded

    Head office adds the distributor in the Admin portal. The distributor gets its own sign-in, and its data stays scoped to it.

  2. Admin portal

    Step 2: Product and pricing masters

    Products with licence and manufacturer fields, HSN-based GST, item groups and pricing by product and customer group are set up once.

  3. Distributor portal

    Step 3: Purchase and stock in

    Raise a purchase order and receive goods against it. Receiving creates batches with manufacturing and expiry dates and posts stock-in to the ledger.

  4. Distributor portal

    Step 4: Sales and invoicing

    Confirm a sales order, deliver it with first-expiry-first-out allocation, then invoice with GST. Returns and credit notes link back to the original.

  5. Distributor and Admin portals

    Step 5: Payments and reports

    Record receipts and payments. Ledgers, trial balance, balance sheet, outstanding and ageing show where the business stands.

Common questions

Short answers based on what the application does today.

See all questions
What is e-Pulse?

e-Pulse is a web application for pharmaceutical distributors. It manages batch-wise inventory and expiry, sales and purchase documents, returns, accounts and head-office oversight, with an optional ERP integration layer.

Who can sign in, and what are the portals?

There are two portals with separate sign-ins: a Distributor portal for day-to-day operations and an Admin portal for head-office oversight. A Distributor sign-in does not grant access to the Admin portal. There is no separate retailer portal; retailers are master-data records.

How does batch and expiry handling work?

Goods receipt creates batches with manufacturing and expiry dates. Stock is derived from a movement ledger, so balances can be viewed by product and batch. Near-expiry and expired-stock screens help you act early.

What is FEFO?

First-Expiry-First-Out. When stock is delivered against a sales order, batches that expire earliest are allocated first.
